question: The Monetary Policy Committee maintained a hawkish stand on the interest rates. In this context, 'hawkish' stand means __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**interest rates were increased.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• A **hawkish **stand on interest rates means that the** central bank** or **monetary policy committee** is inclined towards raising interest rates in order to control inflation.
 
• This is usually done to prevent the economy from overheating due to** excessive borrowing and spending**, which can lead to inflation.
 
• In contrast, a **dovish stand** on interest rates means that the central bank is more likely to** lower interest rates** to stimulate economic growth and borrowing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **"hawkish"** comes from the idea of a** hawk,** which is known for being **aggressive and vigilant.**
 
• A hawkish monetary policy is characterized by a more **aggressive stance** toward controlling inflation and maintaining price stability.
 
• In contrast, a **"dovish" monetary policy **is named after the image of a dove, which is associated with **peace and tranquility.**
 
• A dovish policy is more focused on stimulating **economic growth and reducing unemployment**, even if it means accepting a higher level of inflation.
